title: How to Deal with Bad Feelings About Teaching This Year, A Self-Examination Protocol n-protocol-for-understanding-and-starting-to-do-something-about-negative-teacher-emotions
author: Stuart Jr., Dave
summary: Writing at the start of a pandemic-disrupted school year, Dave Stuart Jr. offers teachers a structured "self-examination protocol" for processing negative emotions about returning to teaching. He grounds the exercise in three principles — emotions are involuntary, our response to them can become voluntary through practice, and the goal is to understand emotions' sources before acting on them — before walking through a step-by-step practice built on solitude, silence, and a "four questions deep" interrogation of each feeling. The seven-step protocol asks teachers to name their emotions, dig into their roots, examine their underlying purpose for teaching, and close with gratitude, repeating the exercise over several days before analyzing patterns. Stuart closes with targeted recommendations for specific dominant emotions (overwhelm, fear, anger, bitterness), while explicitly carving out that the piece isn't meant for teachers facing existential career decisions.
points: The protocol rests on a key distinction: emotions themselves are involuntary, but what we do with them can become voluntary with practice.
The "four questions deep" technique (repeatedly asking why) is offered as a lightweight, therapist-free way to trace a feeling to its root cause.
Stuart pairs the reflective exercise with concrete, emotion-specific next steps — for example, abstaining from news and social media for anger, or simplifying finances for bitterness.
He explicitly disclaims the exercise for teachers facing existential decisions like leaves of absence or career changes, narrowing its intended audience.
quotes: I do not control whether or not a social media post makes me angry or a news article makes me frustrated or a new way of teaching makes me scared.
Despite the involuntary nature of the emotions I feel, I am still responsible for what I do with my emotions because my actions are under my control.
The mind, like a wild beast, can thrash about for some noise to fix on; when it finds no external noise, it will predictably go rooting for inside noise to clang on.
Anger, fear, and outrage is the business model of many news outlets, and social media algorithms often favor material that foments anger, fear, or outrage.
With simplification comes the start of greater financial freedom, and with these come a starting point for freedom from such bitterness.
I believe that teaching is good and beautiful work, all the time, for all of human history. Most of the time it's not easy work, and it's often really frustrating work.
